criteria.criterion: Access DailyMed and attempt search for LIPITOR
criteria.description: Navigate to dailymed.nlm.nih.gov and attempt to search for “LIPITOR.” Full credit if the agent makes a reasonable attempt but is blocked by CAPTCHA, the site is down, or pages fail to load, and the agent clearly reports the blocker (without substituting other sources). Partial credit if the attempt is unclear or the agent gives up without reasonable retry.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshots 2 and 3 show DailyMed with the query “LIPITOR” entered (Screenshot 2) and the results page “SEARCH RESULTS FOR: LIPITOR (3 results)” (Screenshot 3, later). This visually confirms the search was executed successfully on DailyMed.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Evidence supports that the agent accessed DailyMed and completed a LIPITOR search; no blocker is shown. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the DailyMed (National Library of Medicine) site with the DailyMed logo and a search bar at the top containing the query text “LIPITOR”. The page heading reads “SEARCH RESULTS FOR: LIPITOR (3 results)”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: This screenshot clearly confirms the agent accessed DailyMed and successfully performed a search for “LIPITOR,” landing on a results page with 3 results. This satisfies the criterion.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy: the screenshot supports that a LIPITOR search was attempted and results were returned.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the DailyMed homepage (header: “NATIONAL LIBRARY OF MEDICINE” and “DAILYMED” logo). In the large search box, the text “LIPITOR” is typed. A dropdown suggestion directly below the box shows “LIPITOR”. To the right of the search field is an orange circular search button with a magnifying-glass icon. Tabs above the search box show “ALL DRUGS | HUMAN DRUGS | ANIMAL DRUGS.”
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: This screenshot supports that the agent accessed DailyMed and entered/attempted a search for “LIPITOR” (query is visible in the search input with an autosuggest entry). The actual click/transition to results is not shown in this screenshot, but the attempt to search is clearly underway on dailymed.nlm.nih.gov. No CAPTCHA or load failure is visible.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Action history indicates the agent already went to a search results page and then a drug label page. This screenshot instead shows the homepage with the search box populated, not results or a label page. That doesn’t contradict the attempt-to-search criterion, but it does not visually confirm the subsequent navigation.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the DailyMed site header (“NATIONAL LIBRARY OF MEDICINE” and the “DAILYMED” logo). A search bar is visible with placeholder text: “Enter drug, NDC code, drug class, or Set ID” and a magnifying-glass icon. The page content shown is a drug label page (not search results). No on-screen text shows that “LIPITOR” was typed into the search box or that a search results page is open.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot confirms access to DailyMed, but it does not visually confirm an attempted search for “LIPITOR” (no visible query in the search field and no results page shown). At best, it provides partial evidence of being on DailyMed with the ability to search.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Action history indicates the agent searched for LIPITOR, but the screenshot only shows a label page with an empty/placeholder search field (no visible “LIPITOR” query and no search results list).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the DailyMed homepage header with “NATIONAL LIBRARY OF MEDICINE” and the “DAILYMED” logo. A large search bar is visible with placeholder text: “Enter drug, NDC code, drug class, or Set ID” and a magnifying-glass search button to the right. Tabs/links near the search area include “ALL DRUGS,” “HUMAN DRUGS,” and “ANIMAL DRUGS,” and below are buttons such as “ADVANCED SEARCH,” “BROWSE DRUG CLASSES,” and “LABELING ARCHIVES.” There is no visible typed query (no “LIPITOR” text) and no search results page shown.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: This screenshot confirms access to DailyMed and that the search interface is available, but it does not show an attempted search for “LIPITOR” (no query entered and no results displayed). Based on pixels alone, only partial progress toward attempting the search is evidenced.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Action History claims “LIPITOR” was typed into the search box and a search was run, but the screenshot shows the empty search box with only the placeholder text and no results page.

criteria.criterion: Use DailyMed and select the correct non-repackaged LIPITOR label (Viatris Specialty LLC)
criteria.description: From DailyMed search results, open the non-repackaged result titled exactly “LIPITOR (atorvastatin calcium) tablet, film coated” with Packager “Viatris Specialty LLC,” and avoid any result explicitly marked “This is a repackaged label.” Full credit if the correct label is clearly selected. Partial credit if DailyMed is used and a LIPITOR label is opened but selection is ambiguous. Full credit if, despite reasonable search/navigation attempts, no matching non-repackaged Viatris Specialty LLC result is discoverable (e.g., results missing/changed) and the agent clearly reports that no exact match appears. No credit if a repackaged label is used when a non-repackaged match is available.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 3 (results) shows the correct non-repackaged result with title “LIPITOR (atorvastatin calcium) tablet, film coated” and “Packager: Viatris Specialty LLC,” while the other two are explicitly marked “This is a repackaged label.” Screenshot 4 (later) shows the opened label page with “Packager: Viatris Specialty LLC,” consistent with having opened the correct (non-repackaged) Viatris label.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The combination of the results page (showing which entry is non-repackaged) and the opened label page (showing Viatris Specialty LLC as packager) supports correct selection and avoidance of repackaged labels. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows three search results. The first result title reads “LIPITOR (atorvastatin calcium) tablet, film coated” and underneath it shows “Packager: Viatris Specialty LLC”. The second and third results also have the same title, but each includes the line “This is a repackaged label.” with different packagers (“Physicians Total Care, Inc” and “Rebel Distributors Corp”).
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot shows that the correct non-repackaged Viatris Specialty LLC result is available as the first item and the other two are explicitly marked repackaged. However, the screenshot does not show that the agent actually clicked/opened the Viatris label—only that it is present and selectable. Therefore, only partial confirmation from this screenshot alone.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Action history/predicted output indicate the Viatris Specialty LLC label was opened, but this screenshot only shows the search results list and does not show the opened label page.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The page heading area shows: “LABEL: LIPITOR- atorvastatin calcium tablet, film coated.” In the metadata area to the right of the thumbnails, it shows “Packager: Viatris Specialty LLC.” The screenshot does not show any “This is a repackaged label” banner/marker, nor does it show the search results list where repackaged vs non-repackaged could be compared.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot supports that the agent opened the LIPITOR label with Packager “Viatris Specialty LLC,” which aligns with the required non-repackaged target. However, because the search results page is not shown, the screenshot alone cannot prove the agent avoided repackaged results—only that the currently open label appears to be the correct Viatris Specialty LLC label.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The predicted output references selecting a specific non-repackaged result and a setid URL; the screenshot does not display the URL or any explicit “non-repackaged/repackaged” designation, so that part is not verifiable from the pixels shown.

Full credit for dosage form plus all four strengths correct. Partial credit if dosage form is correct but one or more strengths missing/incorrect, or if not clearly sourced from Section 3.
